Shows the debug-only tools in a match: the CAPTURE button, the REC MACRO button beside Menu, macro play in the pause menu, the HUD\u2019s detail card and console, and the test options below. Leave off to play.

The readout in the top-left corner of a match. Minimal: frames per second. Normal: adds frame time and temperature. Complete: adds CPU, memory and textures on a second line. Also in a match: pause and choose \u201cPerformance HUD\u201d.

Drag a control to move it, pinch it or use the size slider to resize it, and hide the ones you do not use. A control dropped on another steps aside. Also in a match: pause and choose \u201cEdit controls\u201d.
Touch a control to pick it up
For tinkering and troubleshooting. The defaults suit most phones; the Graphics and Performance tabs cover the usual changes.
Every change is kept the moment it is made, and takes effect when the next match starts. Press Back to return to the menu.

This phone looks like %1$s (%2$s; %3$s, %4$d fast cores at %5$d MHz, %6$.1f GB). A preset sets render quality, the heat and GPU-load rules, multisampling, FSR, the frame-rate limit and low-memory mode; change any of them afterwards and the preset reads Custom.
How many pixels are drawn on the screen, as a share of it. The display scales the result up. PES draws at a fixed 1280\u00d7720, so this mostly trades sharpness for battery.
Draws the match at 2x or 3x the console\u2019s 1280\u00d7720 (PES17_SCALE). Needs a lot of GPU; leave at 1x unless the phone has room to spare.
Keeps thin pitch lines from breaking into dashes. Cheap on most phones; turn it off if the match stutters.
The console\u2019s frame is a 60 Hz frame. Locking avoids uneven pacing and saves battery on 90/120 Hz screens.
Draws the match ball this much larger so it is easier to follow on a small screen (PES17_BALL_SCALE). 100% is the original size.

How large the 3D scene is drawn before it is stretched to the frame (PES17_SCENE_SCALE). 75% is the default: about 44% fewer pixels for a picture most players cannot tell apart. Go to 100% on a strong phone.

Match render quality above becomes the most the picture is drawn at. As Android reports the phone heating up (moderate, severe, critical) the picture is lowered, down to 50%, before the GPU is throttled, and raised again as it cools (PES17_HEAT_SCALE). Steps are held a few seconds; one shows as the scene being redrawn for a moment.
Lower quality when the GPU falls behind

Steps the picture down when the render passes take too long for the frame and back up when there is room (PES17_LOAD_SCALE). It only sees GPU pass time, which on the Snapdragon 865 was not what made a slow match slow, so it rarely acts there. Experimental.

Tells Android how long each frame took so it can raise or lower the CPU and GPU clock (PES17_HINT). Does nothing on a phone that refuses it, such as the Snapdragon 865 on Android 13; turn it off if a phone runs hotter with it.

Off leaves the stands empty and spares the renderer and the GPU the crowd\u2019s drawing, which keeps the phone a little cooler in a match. The game still animates it. Takes effect the next time the game starts.
Uses an AMD FSR upscale and sharpen pass instead of a plain stretch. Costs a few frames on a hot phone.

The game draws 30 frames a second and a frame made between each two fills the gaps, so the 60 Hz screen stays smooth for about half the work and heat. Fast movement can look soft. Sets the 30 fps limit while on.

Widens the game\'s camera to the phone\'s shape and fills the whole screen instead of showing black bars at the sides (PES17_ASPECT). Menus and the score bar are stretched sideways. Takes effect on the next start.

Takes the match off the 60 Hz pacing and limits it to this many frames a second (PES17_FPS_LIMIT). Lower is cooler and longer-lasting. On a 60 Hz screen 30 gives the most even motion; 35 to 55 can judder.
Skips the large vertex shadow buffer (PES17_NO_SHADOW). Use it on 6 GB phones or less, or if the match is killed in the background.
Texture memory: chosen for this phone
How much the texture cache may hold before it lets go of what has not been drawn lately. Left alone, the runtime picks a figure from this phone\u2019s memory.
Compiles every recorded pipeline before the title screen instead of during play. Boot takes minutes on a cold cache, but kick-off is free of shader stutter afterwards.
Touch controls stay player 1; the first physical controller drives player 2. Takes effect when a match is started.
Turn off to ignore controllers entirely. Some phones report an accessory as a gamepad with a stick that is not centred, which makes a player run on his own.
The on-screen pad is edited in the match: pause and choose \u201cEdit controls\u201d.
The files stay on the phone; the app simply stops using them, and a new folder can be chosen. If the files are still in a place the app searches, it will find them again on its own.
